intended_object: The forgetful functor Action V G ⥤ V. It sends an object of V with an action of the monoid G (a functor from the one-object category of G into V) to its underlying object, and an equivariant morphism to its underlying morphism. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: On objects the definition sends M to M.V, the underlying object. On morphisms it sends f to f.hom, the underlying morphism of V. This is exactly the forgetful functor from G-objects in V to V. The functor laws hold by definition, because composition and identities in Action V G are computed on the underlying morphisms. The setting is fully general: V is an arbitrary category and G an arbitrary monoid. The "(implementation)" label in the docstring only means that users should go through the `CategoryTheory.forget` API instead of calling this directly. The functor itself is the standard mathematical forgetful functor, and the definition matches it.
